title: 2.2.2 Virtual Reality
description: Definition of VR, 3D sensory simulation, sensory devices, data gloves, force-feedback, and immersion mechanisms from Grade 11 ICT Section 2.2.2.

questions.question: What is Virtual Reality (VR) defined as in the textbook?
options: A technology creating a three-dimensional computer-generated simulated environment
A system overlaying digital statistics upon physical real-world surfaces
A telecommunication method connecting two remote offices via voice line
A database backup procedure copying files to secondary optical disks
questions.correctAnswer: A technology creating a three-dimensional computer-generated simulated environment

questions.question: Which suite of electronic hardware allows a person to interact with VR?
options: Goggles, headsets, gloves, or bodysuits
Flatbed scanners, laser printers, and mice
Surge protectors, transformers, and cords
Line conditioners, modems, and antennas

questions.question: How does Virtual Reality interact with human sensory perception?
options: Presents artificial information to convince minds that simulation is reality
Transmits high-voltage electrical currents directly into nerve endings
Restricts sensory input exclusively to monochromatic command terminals
Eliminates auditory awareness through acoustic soundproofing chambers
questions.correctAnswer: Presents artificial information to convince minds that simulation is reality

questions.question: What level of sensory immersion does Virtual Reality provide to the user?
options: A completely immersive experience
A partially immersive experience
A purely text-based experience
A non-interactive experience

questions.question: How does a VR environment respond when a user moves their head or body?
options: Adjusts perspectives and visual fields in real time using sensors
Pauses program execution until the user returns to center position
Transmits error event logs to the operating system notification tray
Prompts the user to re-enter network credentials using a keyboard
questions.correctAnswer: Adjusts perspectives and visual fields in real time using sensors

questions.question: Which specialized device enables users to physically feel and touch virtual items?
options: Data gloves equipped with force-feedback mechanisms
Standard wireless mice equipped with optical lasers
Capacitive smartphone screens with glass coating
Mechanical keyboards with backlit alphanumeric keys
questions.correctAnswer: Data gloves equipped with force-feedback mechanisms

questions.question: What enables Virtual Reality to create the convincing illusion of physical presence?
options: Real-time sensor tracking combined with tactile force-feedback manipulation
Projecting two-dimensional slide transparencies onto classroom walls
Printing detailed photographic illustrations in high-resolution textbooks
Reading historical descriptive manuscripts inside soundproof library cubicles
questions.correctAnswer: Real-time sensor tracking combined with tactile force-feedback manipulation
